meta.purpose: Each gate exists to remove one specific way a lucky or overfitted strategy can look like skill. A strategy is only promotable when every applicable gate returns PASS from an executed run, not from a promise.
meta.enforcement: Proposed implementation is /tools/gates.py (SG-09). Until then these thresholds are documentation and that is stated on the site.
meta.threshold_convention: A numeric threshold with value null is a deliberate blank: it is a value the reviewer must set (flagged F-05). No default is silently substituted at run time.

gates.name: Sample sufficiency
gates.prevents: Run luck. A 60% hit rate on 40 bets is a coin with a story attached.
gates.test: Count settled bets in the frozen evaluation window; require n >= threshold AND the 95% CI of the primary metric to exclude break-even.
gates.pass_rule: Both n and CI conditions must hold on out-of-sample data.
gates.notes: min_distinct_games matters because 500 bets on 30 games is 30 bets of information, not 500.

gates.name: Walk-forward integrity
gates.prevents: Fitting the answer. Re-tuning inside the evaluation window turns noise into a rule.
gates.test: Split chronologically: fit window, then a frozen evaluation window. Any parameter, feature flag or threshold changed inside the evaluation window voids the run. Config and data hashes are recorded.
gates.pass_rule: Edge present in a majority of folds and in the pooled out-of-sample result.
gates.notes: Fold boundaries must be whole weeks, never random rows, because games in a week share news events.

gates.name: Closing-line-value beat rate
gates.prevents: Attributing a hot streak to skill, and attributing a cold streak to bad luck. CLV is measurable per bet, the day it is placed.
gates.test: For each bet, cents beaten = fair-implied prob at taken price minus at anchor close. Test mean > 0 (one-sided), plus a beat-rate floor.
gates.pass_rule: Mean CLV positive at the corrected alpha and beat rate above floor. min_mean_clv_cents is a blank awaiting the reviewer's cost model (F-05).
gates.notes: CLV is the primary promotion metric by design (SG-06). It is not proof of profit; it is proof of getting better prices, which is the part that compounds.

gates.name: Real cost and capacity
gates.prevents: An edge that exists at $1 stakes and dies at $200.
gates.test: Re-price the whole backtest at the worst acceptable price actually available at the reviewer's stake size, with vig, limits, and void rules; then test at 2x stake.
gates.pass_rule: ROI remains positive at 2x stake after costs, with promo/bonus value explicitly excluded.
gates.notes: Promo value is excluded on purpose: it is real money but it is not a property of the strategy, and counting it hides whether the signal exists.

gates.name: Regime stability
gates.prevents: An edge that is really one season, one rule change, or one soft book.
gates.test: Split the evaluation into disjoint blocks (early/late season, and by year). Require a positive lower confidence bound in each block; measure decay slope.
gates.pass_rule: No block is negative at its own CI and the trend slope is not significantly negative.

gates.name: Risk of ruin and drawdown
gates.prevents: A positive-EV strategy that goes broke before the EV arrives.
gates.test: Simulate the staking rule over the realised bet sequence with resampled outcomes; report max drawdown distribution and probability of losing 50% of bankroll.
gates.pass_rule: Ruin probability below the reviewer-set tolerance; stakes never exceed the cap even when the model is more confident than the cap allows.
gates.notes: acceptable_prob_ruin is blank by policy: the number is a personal risk decision, not a modelling result.

gates.name: Input-error robustness
gates.prevents: Fragility on exactly the field we know is noisy: the game-status designation, which is a club's expectation, not a measured probability.
gates.test: Perturb inputs: flip +/- 1 designation per team, move Questionable to a 50/50 coin, drop the latest snapshot and use the one before it. Re-run the strategy.
gates.pass_rule: At least half the edge survives the perturbation set; otherwise the strategy is a news-speed trade wearing a model costume.
gates.notes: A strategy that only works when you are first to the news is a latency business, not a modelling business. That is a legitimate conclusion - it must be stated, not hidden.

gates.name: Correlation and portfolio exposure
gates.prevents: Hidden concentration: six 'independent' bets that are the same game, the same total, or the same weather.
gates.test: Compute the realised covariance of the strategy's bet set; cap aggregate exposure per game, per side of the same market, and per shared driver (QB start, weather, short week).
gates.pass_rule: Portfolio variance computed with measured covariances, never with independence assumed. Thresholds are blank pending Q-RISK-01.

gates.name: No look-ahead
gates.prevents: Winning backtests by knowing the future.
gates.test: Every field carries published_at. The engine may only read a field when published_at <= bet_ts - safety_margin. A violation raises a hard error. Randomly re-verify 5% of rows against the source page's own timestamps.
gates.pass_rule: Zero violations; any row with unknown publication time is excluded from pricing, not assumed safe.
gates.notes: allow_null_published_at = false is the load-bearing part. Most 'edge' disappears here.

gates.name: Market-microstructure realism
gates.prevents: Assuming we can get the price we saw.
gates.test: Compare the price at signal time to the price actually fillable N seconds later at the target stake; measure slippage and rejection rate.
gates.pass_rule: Fill rate above floor, and the strategy's edge exceeds mean slippage.

gates.name: Multiple-testing correction from the decision journal
gates.prevents: The leaderboard selecting noise: with 40 variants tried, one will clear 5% significance doing nothing.
gates.test: Read the number of variants sharing this hypothesis family from the journal; adjust alpha (Bonferroni at minimum, a deflated-Sharpe style haircut for ROI claims); report the adjusted result.
gates.pass_rule: Survives at the corrected alpha. If the journal is missing or incomplete, the gate fails closed.

gates.name: Economic significance and crowding decay
gates.prevents: A statistically real, economically irrelevant edge that dies the moment it is used.
gates.test: Report cents per bet at target stake, weekly capacity, and a decay estimate by re-running the backtest with the price moved one half-point against us.
gates.pass_rule: Still positive after the adversarial shift, and capacity above the reviewer's minimum.

gates.name: Compliance and source licensing
gates.prevents: Building a business on data or wagers we are not allowed to make.
gates.test: For each source: a recorded terms note and an approval flag. For wagering: jurisdiction and operator licence confirmation. No flag, no ingestion.
gates.pass_rule: All sources approved, or restricted to public aggregate facts with attribution (the mode this site currently runs in).
gates.notes: This build publishes only verified facts from the league's own public pages with a link per row, which is the conservative posture. It does not ingest any price data.

gates.name: Anti-gaming controls on the leaderboard itself
gates.prevents: The competition being won by whoever games the ranking rather than the market.
gates.test: Reject retroactive submissions (ledger is hash-chained and append-only); cap bets per game; forbid two strategies taking the same side of the same price (sample farming); require a pre-registered hypothesis timestamp before the bet; void any row whose price source cannot be re-read.
gates.pass_rule: All checks pass on the immutable log; violations demote the strategy to 'quarantine' rather than delete evidence.

gates.name: Kill switch and pre-registered stopping rule
gates.prevents: Doubling down. The most expensive failure in wagering systems is not a bad model, it is a bad model that is being defended.
gates.test: Before promotion, register the drawdown and CLV-run that ends the strategy. After the trigger fires, the strategy is suspended automatically and can only return through a fresh pre-registered hypothesis.
gates.pass_rule: Not a pass/fail - an always-on monitor that can revoke a promotion.
